idea.name: Lawn care business in Texas
idea.one_liner: A buyer acquires a Texas lawn care business with existing revenue and cash flow, using SBA financing or negotiating seller financing.
idea.customer: Customers needing lawn care in Texas; their type is not specified.
idea.revenue_model: Revenue and cash flow from the existing service business; payment cadence is not stated.

key_quotes.quote: Let's say that we have a lawn care business, that's grass.
It means over the same 10-year window, you're gonna have an additional 135 K in your pocket.

claims.claim: The example business is listed for $349,000, with about $325,000 annual revenue and $144,000 cash flow.
claims.quote: In this lawn care business, it's located in Texas, the asking price for that business is $349,000. It's doing about 325 K a year in revenue and in cash flow, someone in your pocket, about 144 K.

claims.claim: The speaker describes a 44% profit margin, or 44 cents kept per customer dollar.
claims.quote: Well, that's about a 44% profit margin, which basically means when a customer gives you a dollar, you get to keep about 44 cents of every dollar.

claims.claim: The SBA scenario assumes 10% down, about $35,000 on the $349,000 asking price.
claims.quote: Now, if we go to the SBA, they're gonna put 10% down. The asking price for the business is 349 K. So you're gonna put about 35 K down.

claims.claim: The SBA financing example uses a 10-year loan.
claims.quote: Then you're gonna finance that with a 10 year SBA.

claims.claim: The speaker estimates $51,000 in first-year debt service and about $93,000 left in cash flow.
claims.quote: That means in year one, you're gonna have to pay the bank about 51 K. What does that leave you with? About $93,000 in cash flow.

claims.claim: The speaker estimates a 265% cash-on-cash return for the $35,000 down payment.
claims.quote: If you're making 93 K a year, the cash on cash return is 265, oops, 265%.

claims.claim: The seller-financing example offers the seller 40% of profits until $375,000 is repaid, compared with a $350,000 price in the SBA example.
claims.quote: We're gonna say we want 40% of the profits and tell you pay back 375 K, not even the 350 K, you were gonna pay.

claims.claim: The seller-financing example pays back the seller over seven years and is described as saving tens of thousands of dollars.
claims.quote: You're gonna pay it back inside of how many years, seven years, because you're gonna do it faster than the SBA loan and save yourself tens of thousands of dollars.

claims.claim: The seller-financing version has a $35,000 down payment and $375,000 owed to the seller.
claims.quote: Well, that means you would put down that 35 K in order to get this business and you would do a transaction where it's still that you owe the seller the agreed amount, this 375 K

claims.claim: The seller-financing scenario gives the seller 40% of profits until repayment over seven years.
claims.quote: Just old-fashioned, you plus the seller determining this purchase price, having this down payment, and you give the seller 40% of the profits until you pay back the 375 over these seven years.

claims.claim: The speaker estimates an additional $135,000 in the buyer's pocket over the same 10-year window.
claims.quote: It means over the same 10-year window, you're gonna have an additional 135 K in your pocket.

ideas.delivery: A buyer operates the lawn care service and manages its financing. The speaker's example compares bank financing with a seller-financed purchase.

idea.name: Boardroom business growth program

idea.customer: Business owners with six- to nine-figure revenue, according to the speaker.
idea.offer: Help growing businesses improve revenue and profits.

key_quotes.quote: And so we help business owners that are doing at least six figures up to nine figures in revenue, grow their business by 24% each quarter plus.
At something called the boardroom, this is the only thing we obsess on.

claims.claim: The speaker says business growth can produce a valuation or asset increase of two to ten times the increase in the business.
claims.quote: You can actually get a valuation or asset increase of anywhere from two to 10x.

claims.claim: The speaker gives an example of doubling a business's value from $100,000 to $200,000.
claims.quote: So if you have a business right now and you can double the value of the business from $100,000 to $200,000.

claims.claim: The example says that a $100,000 increase in business value could mean a $200,000 to $1 million increase in overall value.
claims.quote: That means you didn't increase it by $100,000. You actually increased it by $200K, two, in some cases, a million dollars plus.

claims.claim: The speaker says Boardroom helps businesses with six to nine figures in revenue grow by 24% or more each quarter.
claims.quote: And so we help business owners that are doing at least six figures up to nine figures in revenue, grow their business by 24% each quarter plus.
